newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says not offended by Sen Lott's criticism.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says not offended by Sen Lott's criticism.

text.p: President Clinton said Friday he was not offended by Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott's criticism of his proposed budget, and said that he knew all along it would be difficult to achieve a compromise.
"I took no offense by what he said," Clinton told reporters during a picture-taking session with visiting Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

"We always knew we were going to have to work hard to reconcile our differences. We can do this," Clinton said. "If you look at the differences between us and you look at how close we are to a balanced budget, we can do it and I'm convinced we will do it."
"What I want to do is make sure we do it in a way that is best for the American people," he added.
Clinton said he had spoken to Lott by phone and tried to "put him in a better frame of mind," after Lott said he was very depressed by Clinton's proposed budget.
Clinton said that, overall, he was encouraged by comments from House and Senate Republican leaders.
